  - text: S1
  - heading "Summary" [level=2]
  - text: Generated · 30-second read
  - paragraph: Executive overview of what this item covers, key takeaways, and how its timeline and scope affect freight operations.
  - paragraph: Regulation (EU) 2024/3005 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 November 2024 on the transparency and integrity of ESG rating activities, published in the Official Journal of the European Union. It makes ESG rating providers operating in the Union subject to authorisation, recognition or registration by ESMA, with disclosure, conflict-of-interest and complaints rules, and applies from 2 July 2026.
  - paragraph: Why it matters
  - paragraph: ESG ratings are used by investors, borrowers and issuers, and by undertakings that buy them to assess risks and opportunities within their operations, so the companies that sell them now sit under ESMA supervision from 2 July 2026. A rated company can raise factual errors and the way a method was applied through the provider's complaints route, and a buyer can look up a provider on a public ESMA register, which gives a basis to check a score that a customer cites. A provider that infringes the Regulation faces a fine of up to 10 % of its total annual net turnover; the text states no charge or surcharge passed to buyers or rated companies, so no cost reaches a freight invoice from the text alone. The duties fall on rating providers and the text names no freight role, so a freight operator's exposure is as a buyer of a rating or as a company that is scored.
  - paragraph: What it changes
  - paragraph: From 2 July 2026 ESG rating providers operating in the Union need ESMA approval and appear on a public register, so buyers and rated firms can check a provider and complain.
  - paragraph: Key data
  - paragraph: Applies from 2 July 2026
  - paragraph: Providers already operating notify ESMA by 2 August 2026; small providers by 2 November 2026
  - paragraph: Fine ceiling 10 % of total annual net turnover of the ESG rating provider
  - paragraph: Providers submit public information to the European single access point from 1 January 2028
